result.shared_observations: All options must effectively address the need for a distress signaling system.

result.system_overview: The target system operates as a distress signaling mechanism for a volunteer kayak patrol in a coastal town. The kayakers, who are out for 2-3 hours, rely on a lightweight check-in/check-out system that functions effectively even with limited cellular signal and without constant GPS tracking. The current system, which involves sending a group text to indicate launching, is ineffective as it is often ignored. Therefore, the new system must ensure that distress signals can be sent passively and without the need for active engagement from the kayakers, especially in case of incapacitation.

Reinforcing.Description: Increased usage of the distress signaling system leads to higher awareness and responsiveness among the patrol members.
Assumptions: Increased awareness leads to more timely responses
More frequent use improves system reliability

Balancing.Description: The need for privacy limits the frequency of distress signals that can be sent.
Assumptions: Privacy concerns will limit the acceptance of constant monitoring
